launches.title: Browser Use: Open Source alternative to OpenAI Operator
launches.tagline: We enable AI to control your browser.
launches.body:
Hey everyone, we're Gregor and Magnus we are excited to launch Browser Use Cloud!

# What is Browser Use (Cloud)?

We started this project 3 months ago because it simply wasn’t possible to use the Browser with any LLM. We thought “How hard could it be to build the interface between LLMs and the web?” Fast forwarding 3 months, we have combined 25k ⭐ on Github and our Open Source community is growing fast.

Four days ago, OpenAI launched Operator. Since then, our community has been asking non-stop for a hosted version of browser-use. So we shipped that. Now you can use Browser Use as a B2C chat tool at <https://cloud.browser-use.com/>. We are releasing the API in the next few days. If you need API access for web agents, call us, don’t wait for the Open AI Operator API to be released!

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=87243&key=user_uploads/1367312/bc5949c1-a906-4131-a621-d7da318dda1a)

# Existing problems

During many conversations with our discord community of 5000 people, we identified these core challenges in browser automation:

* Websites change, and this breaks automation scripts. You usually only notice this, when it's too late.
* Websites often catch bots. To avoid this, you need to use different IP addresses, solve captchas, and act more like a human.
* Many people get frustrated with rate limits, parsing errors and API key management, when they do LLM-based scraping.
* The most useful tasks often require you to log in. This can be a pain, especially if you have to type in your username and password every time.

[Browser Use hosted version](https://cloud.browser-use.com/) addresses these challenges by handling proxy rotation, maintaining persistent sessions - so you only need to login once, and allowing you to run as many instances in parallel as you need. We've priced it at $30/month, significantly lower than Operator.

On the open-source side, browser-use remains free and flexible. You can use any LLM you prefer - from Gemini to Sonnet, Qwen, and even DeepSeek-R1. It comes with an MIT license and full customisation options.

This week, we're working on follow-up questions, task reruns, voice mode, and scheduled agent starts. If you want to build automations directly into your products call us, we are happy to explore your use cases and help you set get set up with the API or even custom integration.

**Our vision is simple**: tell your computer what to do, and it gets it done.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=87243&key=user_uploads/1367312/1ac17208-7147-4696-aa13-7e67a4be8329)

We'd love to hear from you. What automation challenges are you facing? How do you think people will interact with computers in the future?

launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋

We’re [Brontë](https://www.linkedin.com/in/bronte-kolar/) and [Tahir](https://www.linkedin.com/in/tahirdme/) – co-founders of [Zeon Systems](https://www.zeonsystems.ai/). We’re on a mission to make science move at the speed of thought.

# **TL;DR**

**We turn natural language into lab automation.** Scientists type their experiment in English. Our software programs robots to execute it.\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x-jid99QPFA>

# **Problem**

The biggest scientific breakthroughs -- _think Selman Waksman mining microbes for antibiotics or Akira Yoshino testing early lithium-ion batteries_ _at Sony_ -- started in labs through painful, manual work. **Decades later, discovery still relies on pipetting, weighing, and prepping by hand.**

It’s inefficient, exhausting, and slows down discovery. Automation solutions exist, but are often **$$$** or built for **specific use cases**. 

We want to change that.

# **Our Take**

What if you could run an experiment by just typing it out? 

That’s what we’re building for: **automation that’s usable by everyday scientists.**

# **The Zeon System 🦾**

We sell a hardware + software system that runs lab experiments using off-the-shelf robotics. **Labs receive a ready-to-run automation setup** that includes:

* Our AI-powered software
* 2 off-the-shelf robotics arms with mounted depth cameras

_How it works:_

* Scientists describe protocols in plain English
* Zeon interprets them, detects lab tools using computer vision, and plans the execution
* The system generates and executes robotic code in real-time, adapting to the specific lab environment

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=89951&key=user_uploads/379901/f18d8421-74dc-4213-8f17-a91419504529)

# **What’s Possible**

We are already piloting with labs at UCSF and Stanford to:

* Run fluorescence screens for nanoparticles overnight
* Automate multichannel pipetting for clinical assays
* Dispose of biohazardous waste while researchers sleep

# **Big Picture**

Eventually, we want to **enable labs that run themselves**. Think self-driving labs on Mars or in the middle of the ocean doing science while humans dream. 🪐 🧪🧬

# **The Team**

[Brontë](https://www.linkedin.com/in/bronte-kolar/) built electronic systems for electric aircraft and high-density battery packs before pivoting to computational biology research at UCSF, UC Berkeley, and Erasmus Medical Center. 

[Tahir](https://www.linkedin.com/in/tahirdme/) has been building software and ML for science labs basically all his adult life, doing computational research at IIT, Yale and working in biotech and pharma across India and the US.

launches.body:
Hey friends [👋](https://emojipedia.org/waving-hand)

This is [Xavier](https://www.linkedin.com/in/xavierchi/) and [Sebastian](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sebbyjp/) - Co-Founders of Mbodi AI, and we are making robots learn like humans.

# **TL;DR**

**We’re building an embodied AI platform that lets anyone teach robots new skills — just by talking to them.** No code. No engineers. No week-long reprogram. Mbodi turns natural language and quick demos into precise, reliable robot actions that run in production in minutes, and adapt as often as you need.

We are now rolling out real-world deployments to customers with a joint commercialization partner, [ABB](https://new.abb.com/products/robotics), the world’s leading robot manufacturer.

https://youtu.be/CwRxP3_F9MA

# 🚨 **The Problem**

Manufacturing is facing a critical inflection point.

**Labor crisis:** Labor accounts for nearly half of global GDP ($40+ trillion), but over 70% of factories face severe labor shortages.

**Flexibility gap:** Traditional robots require week-long reprogramming by engineers or specialists every time things change.

**Untapped automation potential:** Hundreds of billions of dollars in manufacturing tasks, especially those with high variation, remain out of reach for automation because robots can’t adapt fast enough.

This mismatch, between inflexible robots and ever-shifting production needs, leaves a massive automation gap across global manufacturing. We simply need robots to be more **versatile**. It wasn’t quite possible — **until now**.

# **🧠 How Mbodi AI Helps**

Mbodi is an embodied AI platform that makes robots learn like humans, with natural language. So anyone can teach robots new skills by talking to them and execute the learned skills reliably in production, in minutes.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=90633&key=user_uploads/1111983/cd7897e7-4fc9-4137-8c3d-2b6fe0b487bb)

We’ve built a cloud-to-edge system that takes your instructions, understands the environment, makes a plan, and turns it into precise, safe robot actions. All within a second. Our universal agent framework can run across any robotic hardware, coordinating perception, reasoning, planning, and control in real time.

* 🕐 No week-long reprograms
* 👷‍♂️ No on-site engineers
* 🗣️ Just say what you want done
* 🏭 Run reliably in production

When one robot learns something, the entire fleet does. Individual skills can be reused, repurposed, and adapted instantly — across machines, factories, and tasks.

# 🚀 **What’s Happening**

We’re moving toward real-world deployments after entering a joint commercialization agreement with ABB Robotics, one of the world’s leading robot manufacturers, following our win in their global AI Startup Challenge from among hundreds. This represents a first-of-its-kind system in industrial automation.

We’re building toward a world where robots are as easy to teach and adapt as software — turning them into true consumer commodities and making automation accessible to every factory and beyond.

# 📣 **Our Ask**

If you're a **manufacturer**, **system integrator**, or **robot maker** exploring more flexible and intelligent automation, we’d love to connect and solve automation challenges that were previously out of reach.

Reach us at: [**founders@mbodi.ai**](mailto:founders@mbodi.ai)

We’re also strong advocates of the open-source community. We open-sourced one of our libraries, [embodied-agents](https://github.com/mbodiai/embodied-agents), to enable seamless integration of transformer models into robotics stacks, with more open-source projects coming in the future.

# 👥 **The Team**

[Sebastian Peralta](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sebbyjp/) is a physicist, roboticist, and deep learning researcher. Before Mbodi, he was a core engineer at Google Public DNS (8.8.8.8), and earned a triple major (EE, CS, Physics) from UPenn, where he also conducted graduate research at the GRASP Robotics Lab.

[Xavier (Tianhao) Chi](https://www.linkedin.com/in/xavierchi/) is a former tech lead of Google Public DNS (8.8.8.8), one of the world’s most critical internet services, with work featured in[ The Register](https://www.theregister.com/2023/01/19/google_dns_queries/) and topping[ Hacker News](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=39960125). He holds bachelor's and master's degrees in ECE from UIUC.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=90633&key=user_uploads/1111983/87381bac-5704-43f6-9fa3-1796b4af0f53)

We started Mbodi after seeing robots fall short of their potential — stuck in brittle code and long deployment cycles. With breakthroughs in generative AI and agentic systems, we’re building a future where robots can truly learn, adapt, and scale.

launches.body:
**Problem** 🔴

Too often, customers tell us they use Stripe for billing but when I ask how they manage their credits or track usage, I always hear the same answer: “we built it in-house”. These pricing models are not edge-cases. They’re the new normal in the age of AI.

**Solution** ⚒️

[uselark.ai](https://uselark.ai) is a modern billing platform with the flexibility to support any pricing model (credit-based, usage-based, hybrid, dimensional, token-based, etc…) at any scale (**10x more** than Stripe).

Whether you’re building an AI powered API or a B2B SaaS product, Lark provides everything (including checkout + customer-facing portal) you need to implement complex billing logic without the hassle.

A few nice things about us -

* You don't have to manage any webhooks or store custom billing state (like stripe customer id) in your database
* Our APIs are simple. You don't have to integrate with a separate checkout API. We also provide [frontend SDKs](https://docs.uselark.ai/guides/subscriptions/feature_access/) to check billing state (like remaining credits, feature access)
* Seamless pricing changes that automatically apply to your customers without involving engineers
* We also help you track margins & LLM costs per customer for AI applications

📘 **Quickstart**: https://docs.uselark.ai/

launches.title: Slashy - start saving 2 hours a day on email
launches.tagline: Slashy drafts replies in your voice, schedules meetings, and handles follow ups, so you spend less time managing email, and more time on what matters
launches.body:
Hey everyone we’re Harsha and Dhruv from Slashy. Our goal is to define the next generation of email, by building an email platform that actually works for you, and learns over time. \
\
**TLDR:** Slashy is the next big email platform after Superhuman, the first with an assistant built in. Slashy can do everything from writing drafts in your tone, texting you when an important email comes in, prepping you for calls, to the things you expect from a true email client like keyboard shortcuts, open tracking, a mobile app and more. All while continuously learning about you and your preferences, so it only gets better over time. The average user takes 5 minutes to get set up and saves an extra hour a day. Read an independent review from Tom’s guide (1m+ subscribers) [here](https://www.tomsguide.com/ai/slashy-is-the-ai-email-app-replacing-notion-mail-heres-why).

You can get started for free at [slashy.com](http://slashy.com), and use our YC deal for a long-term discount.

**Launch Video:** <https://youtu.be/o2TN-wwCYm8>

## **Problem**

Most founders we speak to, have one of two problems (sometimes both)

1. They spend too much time manually handling email, and not enough building their company.
2. They don’t spend enough time on email, and lose important deals/hires due to things slipping.

## **Solution**

That’s why we built Slashy, the first email platform that reliably gets work done for you, whether it be drafting emails, notifying you when a prospect replies, schedule meetings, or more. Slashy works wherever you work best, so onboarding is seamless (just ask some of our users). It takes 10 minutes to set up, and saves the average email power user an extra one hour a day. It does this by:

1. **Doing all the basic things right:** Stuff like keyboard shortcuts, open tracking, unified inbox, team comments, availability links, all come part of Slashy. So you don’t lose anything transitioning from Gmail, Superhuman, Front and more. ([@Jayme Hoffman](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/60463) actually switched to Slashy being surprised just that a new email client could match the speed, shortcuts of something like Superhuman)
2. **Writing drafts that sound like you:** Claude drafts sound like slop because they just look at the thread. Slashy does a lot more, it looks at the linkedin/web of recipients, past emails you’ve sent, past changes you’ve made to prior drafts, and more including using our own custom-built memory system for email. (Fun fact we have a special tool for handling suggesting times/scheduling as base llms are very bad at this). ([@Michelle Marcelline](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/379052) pretty much just hits send on all her Slashy drafts with minimal edits)
3. **A powerful sidebar:** Slashy comes with a cursor-like sidebar. That lets you do things like search, draft, schedule and more. So you no longer need to keep flipping between ChatGPT and your email. ([@Yahia Bakour](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2538368) loves this to power thorugh drafts and replies)
4. **Integrations:** Slashy connects to not just your email, but your meeting notes (Granola, Fathom, Circleback, etc.), crm (Attio, Hubspot, Salesforce, etc.), Notion and more since the context to handle email isn’t just in email. ([@Pavlos Markesinis](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2511438) loves how Slashy connects to his Attio and makes life simple)
5. **Automations:** The best assistants also know when to handle things in the background. So Slashy can also automatically do things like prep you for calls, text you when an important email comes in, and more. ([@Owen Botkin](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2579867) relies on Slashy to prep him from calls, and [@Pranav Madhukar](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/1531197) doesn’t even check his email anymore unless Slashy alerts him an email comes in)
6. **iMessage/Slack Bot:** One of the worst parts of traditional clients? You need to open them to see if something important comes in. Slashy can ping you on text/slack so you don’t even need to context switch. (@devansh is one of our bigger Slack fans, while [@Abhinav Gopal](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/979064) for iMessage).
7. **Voice:** Sometimes it’s easier to speak your mind than write (or you’re driving and just can’t haha). So Slashy lets you dictate your thoughts, and our AI will make it sound like a much better version of you. Or you can talk with our voice to voice agent when you’re commuting (@vishruth is one of our power users for our voice drafts).
8. **Personalized Memory:** Slashy gets better the more you use it. It keeps notes on how you write, who you talk to, when you schedule, and also it learns from every edit you made before hitting send. It even once a week goes back and rewrites its notes to better match you. After all you'd expect a human assistant to be smarter after a few months, why not your ai one. ([@Devraj Gopal](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2057015) loves how Slashy has grown to know him more and more).
9. **Natural Language Labels:** A common complaint we hear is the rise of the AI SDR, and how everyone’s inbox is inundated with emails. The problem with traditional labelling systems is they don’t adjust over time, leading to important emails getting missed. Slashy’s labelling system does, leading to a much better filtering rate, and fewer dropped balls. ([@Nazli Danis](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/520906) was drowning in spam before Slashy)

## Security and Privacy

We take security/privacy as an email client very seriously.  We’ve already gotten CASA, and SOC II. We also get monthly pen-tests done by [@Casco](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/30477) to ensure our users' data is safe. None of our AI providers train on your data as well.

## Getting Started

Now if you want to get started just go to[ slashy.com](http://slashy.com), or you can book a time here if you’d like me to demo the product/ask any questions just shoot an email to [founders+ea@slashy.com](mailto:founders+ea@slashy.com), and Slashy will schedule a time that works for both of us :)

launches.body:
**TLDR;** Notte provides a platform to build and deploy web AI agents that don’t break. We turn messy, repetitive web tasks into reliable, self-healing workflows so businesses can scale automation with confidence.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uwTOpQTUfyk

**Context**

We built Notte because the web was made for humans, not AI agents. Our first product was a perception layer that helps LLMs parse and understand site structure, boosting agents’ performance. But 90% isn’t enough to scale enterprise workflows with confidence.

**Agent Workflows**

That’s why we launched **Agent Workflows** - where web automation meets agentic reasoning. Start an agent to discover the workflow, freeze the routine into deterministic steps, and keep agents only where it’s needed to unlock new capabilities. If a site changes, agents dynamically close the gap to ensure workflows never break.

Less tokens = Less expensive = More control = Faster automation

**Full-stack Ecosystem**

* **Hosted Sessions** - Stealth mode and auto-scaling browser
* **Vaults** - Credentials, MFA tokens, SSO, and cookies securely
* **Personas** - Emails and phone numbers for account creations
* **Payments** - Credit card payments and agentic transactions
* **Misc** - File IO, Replays, CDP compatibility, etc.

launches.title: Caddy: The Voice Interface for Your Computer
launches.tagline: Changing how people work across their computer and apps with voice
launches.body:
Hey everyone, we’re [Connor](https://www.linkedin.com/in/connor-waslo/) and [Rajiv](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rajivsancheti/).

We led Loom’s AI suite and saw firsthand how natural language was changing how people work. Now we’re building Caddy, the voice interface for your computer that lets you automate work across all your apps.

Join the waitlist at [trycaddy.ai](http://trycaddy.ai)

**Launch video:** https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v1HwM9mBYHU

### **The problem**

Work today happens across a maze of apps. Slack for messaging. Linear for tickets. Gmail for communication. Calendar for scheduling. Every task requires jumping between tabs and tools.

Even with AI everywhere, we are still using the same old interfaces. Voice assistants like Siri or Alexa can answer trivia but cannot do real work. They do not understand what is on your screen, what app you are in, or what you mean when you say “follow up on this.”

The result is constant context switching, lost flow, and hours wasted on work that should happen automatically.

### **What we are building**

Caddy lives on your desktop and lets you operate your computer with your voice. It has two simple modes.

**Action mode:** You speak your intent, and Caddy takes action.

Ask Caddy to create a ticket in Linear, send a message in Slack, or schedule a meeting in Calendar. Caddy sees what is on your screen and connects it to your apps, so you can stay focused on the work that matters.

**Dictation mode:** Never type again

Write emails, respond to messages, or leave comments anywhere text input exists. It is a direct replacement for typing that works globally across your computer.

Together, these two modes let you automate work and control your computer completely with your voice.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=95249&key=user_uploads/2945950/d99dbe1c-8793-4405-a7ca-568f05c831fd)

### **Who Caddy is for**

We are starting with founders, operators, productivity power users and the voice first generation who spend their days moving between tools and losing time to repetitive work. If that sounds like you, we would love to get you early access.

To join our waitlist add your email at [trycaddy.ai](http://trycaddy.ai) or shoot us a message [founders@trycaddy.ai](mailto:founders@trycaddy.ai)

### **The team**

Before starting Caddy, [Connor](https://www.linkedin.com/in/connor-waslo/) and [Rajiv](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rajivsancheti/) spent four years at Loom where they led product and design for Loom’s AI suite and core product.

Robotic factories building robots. Today we have a 12,000 sqft factory in the Bay Area manufacturing everything from full humanoids to robots for the International Space Station.

Our thesis: Revitalizing domestic manufacturing means driving costs down through automation. We are building an autonomous factory that is able to autonomously process a new order end to end from prototyping to large batch production. That means supply chain management, design for manufacturing, industrial machine retooling, robotic adaptation, quality inspection, packaging, and logistics all automated. Goal: Create a factory that can autonomously go from placed customer order to completed unit scale manufacturing run in 24 hours.

We are currently manufacturing production runs from top labs, full humanoids, and even have a partnership to manufacture robotics for the International Space Station. We've also built supply chain relationships in electronics, actuators, SMT, computing, pneumatics, and raw material suppliers.

A snippet of some of our machines in the factory:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112228&key=user_uploads/2763027/777065e0-e83d-4501-8799-8c490e883851)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112228&key=user_uploads/2763027/30775e59-e171-4949-b959-3dc06ffa5322)

## **Manufacturing at the Core**

This isn't just a robotic manipulation company. Its a manufacturing company.

Internally we have pipelines autonomous building large databases of actuators, and raw tracking and trying to predict what items will need to order now to meet our next day targets.

## **The Harness**

The entire factory is a data harness we can "backprop" learnings through from errors in the customer designs, failed supply chain prediction, slow retoolings, to inaccurate robotic manipulation. Our core belief is that robotic machine learning should not rely on human data to scale but instead learn to improve from its own mistakes in the real world in real time. This closes the manufacturing data gap that currently limits large-scale factory automation.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112228&key=user_uploads/2763027/2baf7c74-80e3-49bb-a6bf-712ce0fb30fc)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112228&key=user_uploads/2763027/4ed0acb3-e1bc-4210-b4d0-b3f3614bc8da)

## **Any Robot Anywhere**

Our thesis is simple. We should be able to make an robot for any environment whether that be a humanoid for the factory floor or a robot for Low Earth Orbit. We currently have a partnership with the ISS to manufacture a robots for the space station.

NASA Houston, Johnson Space Center

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112228&key=user_uploads/2763027/e4558cfa-cf98-447a-acaf-7e83650e73a7)

## **Team**

At heart we're a team of Roboticists. Before Tensr we were the leads for a Berkeley lab's autonomous racing team where we raced autonomous full-scale IndyCars at over 160mph as the ML, Sim, and Robotic Controls leads.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112228&key=user_uploads/2763027/c3772faa-f515-4ee0-b32e-2e586b3ae8e3)

We previously worked in industrial automation, aerospace manufacturing, medical device manufacturing, Berkeley AI Research (BAIR), physics simulation, and secured $17M+ in DARPA / industry sponsorship for UC Berkeley / Stanford research.

Our founding engineers range from Berkeley Robotics PhD, ex-NASA, to 10+ years of manufacturing experience.

## A Better World

On a personal note, not only do I believe we have the opportunity to build a great business but also to make a positive impact on the world. Automate away environmentally harmful materials, eliminate waste 0.1% at a time, and drive steady-state COGS toward only the fundamental inputs (materials and electricity), unlocking strong margins while collapsing the price of everyday goods / cost of living.

Lets build a better world :)

A full view of our vision here:[ tensr.com/whitepaper](https://www.tensr.com/whitepaper)

launches.title: Tensr: Building Autonomous Robotic Factories
launches.tagline: Building fully autonomous robotic factories that make scaling hardware as effortless as scaling on AWS
launches.body:
We're building fully autonomous robotics factories at Tensr to create the AWS of manufacturing. Our factories will receive on-demand orders from customers and spin up robots to operate industrial machinery, package, and ship the finished product all in 24 hours.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=95506&key=user_uploads/2763027/704a7eb3-1ffc-4fc3-b806-32f3fd256418)

[**https://youtu.be/HLijIfoDfpA**](https://youtu.be/HLijIfoDfpA)

**Problem**

Moving fast in manufacturing today doesn't exist. Iterating designs for manufacturing takes months of back and forth getting samples from China and pre-ordering manufacturing capacity several months before the holiday rush, only then to wait several weeks for shipping praying there isn't a strike at the docks. At the same time we see the complete collapse of America industrial capacity as American workers and experience leave the field and contracts are sent overseas.

**Solution**

With the robotics revolution, for the first time it is possible to fully reimagine the factory floor - moving from rigid lines to modular stations, even in high mix settings. However, we believe that automating manufacturing is more than just deploying a foundation model or a humanoid into an existing factory.

Factories need to be designed from the ground up _around_ robots, not the other way around.

Over the past few weeks we turned our living room into an autonomous factory floor, with stations for CNC, moving stock, and a focus on assembly. After demo day, we'll expand to a full manufacturing facility, and start supporting batch orders of all sizes from other companies throughout the country. Currently we also are in talks to provide our own assembly models to other distributors.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=95506&key=user_uploads/2763027/706f70f4-47a7-4466-8281-5cf6d081da43)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=95506&key=user_uploads/2763027/e6420b31-3e74-49d3-b751-c901c5379665)

**Team**

We're a battle-hardened team of UC Berkeley graduate robotics researchers (from Berkeley AI Research (BAIR)) who met in a lab, previously worked on and managed multiple DARPA contracts and led an autonomous IndyCar team where we raced full scale autonomous Indycars at 160mph (250kmh) as the Machine Learning, Simulation/Team Manager, and Robotics Control leads respectively.

\- [Eric Berndt](https://x.com/ekberndt) - MS/BS EE/CS, UC Berkeley, CoFounder + CEO

\- [Adith Sundram](https://www.linkedin.com/in/adithsundram/) - MS/BS ME, UC Berkeley, CoFounder + CTO

\- [C.K. Wolfe](https://x.com/ckwolfeofficial) - Current PhD AI/Robotics, UC Berkeley, CoFounder

In addition, our team brings direct operational experience from Rockwell Automation (industrial automation), aerospace manufacturing, and FDA-regulated medical-device production

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=95506&key=user_uploads/2763027/f907544d-cb70-45d2-b043-708a6739e40c)

**Our Ask**

We're offering early manufacturing / prototyping pilots for hardware companies of all sizes as the new year starts and we open our first facility. If you or anyone you know fits in this bucket, reach out to [**founders@tensr.com**](mailto:founders@tensr.com)!

question_answers.question: How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
question_answers.answer:
We (Anas and Pierre-Habté) met at UC Berkeley in 2017 and immediately started working together on tech projects. After co-founding Snipfeed, scaling it to 20+ people, and selling the company in 2024, we knew we wanted to build again together.

The idea for Bravi came from a very personal pain point: my family runs a shutter installation business in France, and I saw firsthand how many calls and leads were missed every day. On top of that, I launched a side business, Volet Dumont, selling shutters online, and experienced the same chaos with quoting and customer communication.

We realized installers were losing 30–40% of potential revenue just from slow follow-ups, missed calls, and disorganized workflows. With our background in automation and product scaling, we decided to tackle it head-on.

That’s how Bravi was born: combining our founder-market fit, validated by hundreds of conversations with installers, with the conviction that AI assistants could transform how home service companies capture and convert leads.

name: Aside
long_description:
Aside is an AI browser that completes real work across the websites you already use. It can sign in through your browser, work inside email, dashboards, internal tools, docs, and spreadsheets, and keep going when a task takes minutes or hours.

Unlike agents that depend on integrations, Aside uses the web the way you do. Browsing history becomes local memory, so it knows which tools and context matter. Its password manager lets agents autofill credentials without exposing secrets to the AI. Sensitive actions like payments, posts, and messages wait for your approval.

We achieved state-of-the-art on agentic browsing benchmarks, surpassing OpenAI and Anthropic's result- Aside ranked #1 across Mind2Web, Odyssey, bu-bench-v1.
one_liner: The browser built to do real work for you

Sales reps often freeze when faced with technical questions. Like:

launches.title: Waddle Labs - Agents that control robots
launches.tagline: Claude Code for robotics - prompt your robot to do physical tasks
launches.body:
Waddle is the Claude Code for robotics. Connect our API to your robot and type a prompt, then our agents write code to achieve the task in \~20 minutes.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107821&key=user_uploads/2132817/afc74f28-33c6-450c-80c3-7f2d263f213d)

### **Our Hypothesis**

Robot intelligence today depends either on large end-to-end VLAs or classical approaches.

\- VLAs are difficult to customise and steer, require huge amounts of data to train, and don’t yet generalise across embodiments and environment. They face limited deployment.

\- Meanwhile, classical approaches are widely deployed for their reliability and explicit control, but are often brittle and costly to redevelop in new setups.

_Does this tradeoff have to be inevitable?_

**Our hypothesis:** By using agents to control robots, we combine the generalisation of VLAs with the speed and reliability of classical approaches. 

### **Our Solution**

Our agents decomposes a goal into subtasks, and completes each subtask by viewing camera feeds, writing control code, and calling models like VLAs. The agent outputs a program that you can run and iterate on by talking to our agents. 

**Where we've been using Waddle internally:**

\- **Create a working policy in 20 minutes** ("Write a program to package the box")

\- **Generate data for model training** ("Pick and place lego bricks at random positions 1000 times")

\- **Facilitate robotics auto-research** ("I am tuning a policy overnight. Reset the scene after each trial”)\
\
Because our agents are LLMs, they inherit properties of the underlying models. Agents and the code they write are inherently generalist, so they work with any robot and any environment without additional data. Moreover, agents excel at long-horizon planning and can decompose a physical goal into subtasks, verify each stage, and re-plan on failure.

**Interested in trying our agents via our preview API?** Sign up at \[our website\](<https://www.waddlelabs.ai/>) or email [founders@waddlelabs.ai](mailto:founders@waddlelabs.ai)

### **Our Research**

Waddle's agents enable new forms of scaling that we are very excited about:

\- **Scaling compositional generalization:** Our agent first wrote the “fold_grasp” skill while flipping a package; another agent later used it to fold a t-shirt. Over time, agents accumulate a library of skills, enabling future agents to compose them and achieve harder tasks.

\- **Scaling multi-robot cooperation:** Imagine an entire fleet of robots collaborating to achieve a task. For VLAs, this is a nightmare. For Waddle, simply hook up more agents. A master agent spawns subagents, coordinating multiple robots working concurrently.

\- **Scaling from scale:** We evaluated Opus 4.8, Fable 5, and GPT 5.6 Sol on a suite of manipulation tasks: larger models with larger thinking budgets consistently produce better policies. As foundation models improve, so do our robots.

### **The Team**

We are @Yiding Song (Vincent) and @Hanming Ye. We met at MIT’s Research Science Institute, where Vincent was working on multimodal astrophysics models and Hanming was researching topology in the math department. Since then, we’ve become roommates at Harvard where we are either doing ML research or breaking robots - usually both.

There will be millions of robots in the future. Our mission is to enable everyone to take part in building them.

Hey everyone, we’re [@Jasper](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2827656) and [@Pieter](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2067100), co-founders of [@Servo7](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/31224). We build simple and rapidly deployed robots for industry work.

**TL;DR**

Today, implementing robotics means redesigning your entire facility around a robot. This is inefficient and unnecessary. With Servo7, you don’t have to do any of that. Our robots adapt to your environment.

<https://youtu.be/AeXYDjMw_qo>

**Problem**

Currently, industry robots are rigid single-purpose machines. Complete floor plans are redesigned around a single robot. As a result, the installation process is complex and inefficient.

This discourages many businesses from pursuing automation at all. That’s a missed opportunity.

**Solution**

Instead of adjusting the floorplan, redesigning the conveyor belts, and the outflow, our robots just work in the existing process.

We’re using AI models to train wheeled humanoids and robot arms. Once the robots are implemented, they’ll keep learning on the job: performing the tasks faster to increase throughput. The implementation of our robots is much faster and easier.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97659&key=user_uploads/2067100/e4f3ba51-26b4-4115-8b48-01502d7b9b6d)

**How we got here**

We have been deploying robots and automating repetitive work for years, even in highly regulated industries like the military and hospitals. But, we also know the slow pain of traditional control methods. So we turned to AI to control robots, and found a much better way. Instead of pre-programming every possible movement, we put the robot to work with just a few demonstrations. We quit our jobs that same day to start Servo7.

Today, we’re working with warehouses and CPG brands to automate their fulfillment.

**Ask**

If you’re working in logistics, assembly, or manufacturing, our robots can help you improve your operations!

Reach out to us at [founders@servo7.com](mailto:founders@servo7.com) to chat. Cheers!

launches.title: Infera – Control Lab Instruments with Natural Language
launches.tagline: Infera turns a plain-English experiment into a validated, instrument-ready run
launches.body:
### **⚡TL;DR**

**Infera is the Claude Code for scientific instruments.** Describe an experiment in plain English, and Infera turns it into a validated, instrument-ready run, handling the protocol logic, vendor scripts, data, and inventory across the instruments your lab already uses. One system, from intent to execution.

### 🤔 **The Problem**

Labs run on hardware from the future and software from the past.

The instruments are extraordinary. Mass specs identify thousands of proteins, flow cytometers read tens of thousands of cells a second, and cryo-EMs image at near-atomic resolution. These are the machines behind biomarker discovery, immunotherapy, structural biology, and drug development. But the software around them still looks like it shipped in 2003, and runs like it.

We've watched labs running \~6 instruments from 3+ vendors write a one-off script for every experiment, stitch outputs together by hand, and track inventory in a Google Sheet someone probably forgot to update last Tuesday. Scientists spend their week being human glue between machines that should already talk to each other.

### **🔍How Infera Works**

[**Demo Video**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3GPze4X7AeA)

**I. Describe the experiment in plain English.** Infera asks the right questions, surfaces edge cases, and checks against your lab’s inventory and instrument state.

**II. Infera turns it into a run, accommodating both manual and automatable steps.** For programmable instruments, it generates vendor-specific scripts, executes, pulls the data back, and runs the analysis. For manual work like pipetting, gels, hand fermentation, etc., it's the context layer underneath: which step you're on, which reagent goes where, what could go wrong, and how others in the lab have run it before.

**III. The knowledge stays.** Every protocol, every validated run, every edge case becomes part of the system and checked against instrument constraints, lab SOPs, inventory, and prior experiments.

That last part is the hard part. It's what general-purpose LLMs can't do, and it's what enables a researcher to trust the output the way they'd trust a trained technician.

### 👩‍🔬 **Team**

Hi! We’re Chloe and Troy, and we're building Infera to close the gap between science and instrumentation.

* Chloe studied Mechanical Engineering at Harvard. She's been building research software and medical devices since before college (Regeneron STS Scholar), including a microfluidic device that detects harmful chemicals in household products, and has been doing research at places like Fred Hutch, Brigham and Women's, Harvard Medical School, and Pacific Northwest National Lab.
* Troy studied Computation & Neural Systems at Caltech, where he held an endowed research fellowship in a top research lab as an undergraduate. He's published two first-author cancer papers, holds a first-inventor agtech patent, and built and sold two companies before Infera.

Between us, we've run experiments by hand, written the scripts, and watched the whole system break when one person leaves. That's the problem we're building Infera to fix.

### **🎯Ask**

We're currently running pilots with Boston-area academic labs and cores. If any of these are you, reach out at [**hello@infera.bio**](mailto:hello@infera.bio):

* **Academic labs and cores:** know a PI or core director in proteomics, genomics, flow, automation, or screening? We'd love an intro, and we're happy to set up a pilot
* **YC founders with wet labs (diagnostics, therapeutics, synbio, tools):** we’d love to meet whoever runs your lab ops
* **Biotech and life sciences folks:** come say hi
* **Instrument manufacturers** whose customers wish the software were better, let's talk

launches.title: Enjamb - The AI Workforce for Biopharma
launches.tagline: Enjamb runs the entire drug program for biopharma teams, from discovery to FDA approval.
launches.body:
Hey YC 👋\
\
We’re Rayan and Maadhav, and today we’re excited to launch [Enjamb Labs](https://www.enjamb.ai/).

<https://youtu.be/5DwdtiLvViM>\
\
**TL;DR**

Enjamb runs the entire drug program for biopharma teams, from discovery to FDA approval. \
\
Pharma runs on decades of closed legacy systems like Benchling, Veeva, Medidata, and SAS, with no AI layer and no MCP to connect agents to them. So we built that connection layer. \
\
Our agents run on top of their existing systems and data, with no migration, and do the work across the whole program: clinical evidence, trial design, statistical programming, and regulatory submissions.\
\
In just 3 weeks since launch, we're already being used by 500+ employees at top pharma companies, including Johnson & Johnson, AbbVie, Bristol Myers Squibb, Merck & Sanofi.

**The Problem: Pharma’s systems have no AI layer**

It costs $2.6 billion and 10+ years to ship a single drug, and most of that isn't the science. It's the work around it, spread across decades of closed legacy systems that don't talk to each other:

* Benchling stores the data
* Veeva holds the documents
* Medidata runs the trials
* SAS does the stats

Agents are **_finally_**  good enough to do real scientific work. But there's no AI layer on these systems, and no MCP to plug an agent into where pharma's data and work actually live.

**So, we built that connection layer we wished existed.**\
\
**What We Offer: Agents that run on top of pharma’s existing systems**

Enjamb invented the fastest way to run a drug program: a single agentic workspace that unifies the evidence, analysis, and regulatory work.

Our agents:

* Synthesize up-to-date clinical evidence from the literature and real-world data to pinpoint the right endpoints and patient populations
* Design trials and run the statistical programming behind them, including SDTM, ADaM, TFLs, and QC
* Draft and audit regulatory documents like INDs, protocols, SAPs, and NDAs

— all in one auditable workspace, with the context carried end to end.\
\
**The results:** Enjamb generates an FDA submission package in **48 hours** instead of 8 months, with **23x fewer errors** than GPT-5.5. And **98%** of the datasets it produces pass Pinnacle 21, the FDA's standard, on the first pass, before a human even reviews.\
\
**And it all runs in the browser**: full Word, Excel, and PowerPoint editors, a Python and R compute environment, 100+ scientific integrations, and 50+ fine-tuned models for in-silico validation. No setup.

\
**Our Story: Two Researchers Who Lived the Problem**

We're **Rayan** (ML/Bio researcher, first-author paper @ JMIR, presented @ SOT and ISCB, beat SOTA by 20%) and **Maadhav** (ex-Dell AI Lab, ex-Broadcom R&D).\
\
We kept hitting the same wall in research: the science was the easy part. Everything around it, the evidence, the analysis, the documents, was fragmented, manual, and disconnected, and the context died at every handoff.\
\
So we built what we always wanted: one workspace where agents carry the context across the entire drug program.

**If no one's going to build it right, we will.**\
\
**Get Started**

* See Enjamb at [enjamb.ai](http://enjamb.ai)
* Or reach us at [rayan@enjamb.ai](mailto:rayan@enjamb.ai) for a demo

launches.body:
Hi everyone, we're Peyton and Michael Marcotte, brothers and co-founders of [Perceptron ML (YC S26)](https://www.linkedin.com/company/perceptronml/). We make law firms AI-native: we build the AI and software a firm needs to scale. Not a product off the shelf, a system built around how your firm already works, where no fact is used until it traces to a real document.

[Perceptron ML (YC S26) Launch Video](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1c-5RUaBQsJWG-6vJsy0O8PLvAcgpuEco/view)

**The problem.** In 2023, two New York lawyers filed a brief written by AI that cited six cases that did not exist. Courts have caught it more than a thousand times since. So most firms went back to doing everything by hand, and by hand the math is brutal: lawyers lose \~40% of their day to work that isn't law, and tens of billions in legal work goes unclaimed every year because firms can't move fast enough to take it.

**What we do.** Every firm's bottleneck is different, and it is never the one on the shelf. So we build what each firm actually needs: intake answered and filed at 2 a.m., demands drafted from the record, records requests chased until they land, deadlines and statutes watched, every hour matched to its matter, clients updated by text before they think to call. Every firm gets something different, but underneath it's all the same platform we built once: our grounding engine, our connectors into the firm's systems, and our agent runtime. That's what lets us build this broadly without being an agency.

**Why you can trust it.** The AI we build doesn't guess. Every fact traces to a real document, verified against the primary source before a model can use it. Click anything, and the original opens.

launches.tagline: We built a computation layer for health insurance that predicts the lowest true-cost coverage for anyone. We will be the national standard for how America chooses coverage, with the only engine that knows both what plans cost and what they actually do.
launches.body:
Hey everyone — we're **Chang and Bryan**, the founders of **Insurf**.

American health insurance is f\*\*\*ed: chosen by guesswork, enforced by denial. We built the engine that fixes both halves.

**TL;DR**

**Surely** computes the lowest-cost plan for anyone. **Inveto** fights denials for real clinics across Texas, Georgia, and California, and each contract-authorized, de-identified outcome becomes coverage data nobody else has. Everything Inveto learns, Surely knows.\
\
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1x5B44OPfZxd-32UBeGT-0a5WVdMf3Jnl](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1x5B44OPfZxd-32UBeGT-0a5WVdMf3Jnl/view?usp=sharing)

**The problem: America picks health plans from one number**

More than 20 million Marketplace enrollees choose coverage off the sticker premium. That guess is expensive.

• In our data, the lowest-premium plan was the lowest-cost option in **0 of 2,000 simulated years**.

• In one example, the cheaper sticker would have cost **$8,052 more** in a single bad year.

• That's one person. Multiply the risk across a family. Across a company.

• This year alone, **four million Americans** found out what their plans actually cost — and walked away from coverage.

We compute.

**Surely — the cost engine**

Surely ranks all plans by what they'll actually cost: premiums, deductibles, drug tiers, networks, out-of-pocket caps. Every number sourced from government filings.

**Inveto — the denial workbench**

Clinics upload a denial and the clinical record; Inveto produces source-cited, physician-signed appeals and supported prior authorizations. Live with real clinics across Texas, Georgia, and California today.

**The moat is the join**

Every contract-authorized Inveto outcome becomes rights-cleared data about what plans actually do, including approvals, denials, appeals; Surely reads all of it. **What plans cost + what plans do. Nobody else has both.**

**Why now**

In 2028, health plans stop renewing automatically: 20 million+ people will re-choose coverage every single year — the largest forced re-shop in the history of American health insurance. $150 billion a year in premiums, re-decided annually.

And employers are next. The federal government projects **800,000 companies and 11 million+ people** will switch to ICHRA, where employees choose their own plans. That's a **trillion-dollar shift**. With Insurf, employers can expect to save **\~$5,000 per employee, per year**.

**Who we are**

Two friends who met during orientation at Brown. Chang got into medical school at 17, then worked a pharmacy counter watching thousands of people pay out of pocket for what they were promised. Bryan placed internationally in CS and physics competitions and has published IEEE research since high school.

**Our ask**

• Tired of overpaying for health insurance?

• Weighing ICHRA, or trying to cut your company's benefits spend?

• Running a specialty clinic buried in denials and prior auths?

See how much your company can save here: [insurf.io/audit](https://www.insurf.io/audit) or email [founders@insurf.io](mailto:founders@insurf.io) — we'll show you exactly what you'd save.

**Everyone sells plans. Nobody prices them. We compute.**

launches.tagline: The operating system for companies that make, move, or sell physical goods
launches.body:
[Bizmark Launch](https://youtu.be/-5g3wv2OE2g)

Hey everyone, we're Rodrigo and Oscar, founders of Bizmark (S26).

**TL;DR:** Bizmark is the operating system for companies that make, move, or sell physical goods. It connects the systems, spreadsheets, and knowledge a company already has, and turns them into optimized decisions and automated workflows: quotes priced in seconds, schedules that reflow when a machine goes down, inventory balanced between service levels and cash. Bizmark adapts to how each company operates, not the other way around. Working product in weeks, not years. Some of the most innovative American companies use Bizmark to transform their operations. Ask: intros to decision makers at manufacturers, distributors, and retailers.

**The problem**

> _“Quotes take too long, so I lose revenue. Or I quote too fast and give away margin.”_

> _“Days of inventory are critical for my business, but I’m not sure I’m buying the right quantities at the right time, or getting the best supplier terms.”_

> _“An urgent order comes in and I do not know what to run next. I’m hitting max capacity constantly, but I’m not sure I’m using my equipment and labor in the most efficient way.”_

After 150 of these conversations, we've realized these problems share the same cause. Legacy ERPs force operators into templates that don’t reflect how the business runs, while custom implementations often run to years and seven-figure budgets. As a result, decisions that directly affect revenue, margins, and service levels are made from spreadsheets, delayed reports, and fragmented tools, with less information than the company has, often by whoever is closest, not whoever knows best.

**What we built**

Bizmark is the operating system for companies that make, move, or sell physical goods. It connects the systems, spreadsheets, and knowledge a company already has, and turns them into optimized decisions and automated workflows. Bizmark adapts to how each company operates, not the other way around. And customers get a working product in weeks, not years.

**Here’s how some of the most innovative American companies use Bizmark to transform their operations:**

A spec-heavy RFQ lands in the inbox. Bizmark reads it, and a quoting engine prices it against inventory, capacity, and customer history. It returns a customer-ready quote in seconds. The team approves it, it goes out, and when the customer says yes, the order enters the system without any retyping.

Then the order runs. Bizmark schedules it into your machines and crews against your objectives, using the same estimates the quote was priced on. When a machine goes down or a rush order lands, the plan reflows and the new sequence reaches the queues that run the operation. The job runs, passes quality, and ships.

The order drew down inventory. Bizmark forecasts what you will sell next, holds your days of inventory in balance – enough for minimum service levels while protecting cash – and decides what to buy, when, and from whom. It sends RFQs to qualified suppliers and compares what comes back. The team chooses, and the PO books straight into the system.

**Who we are**

We’re cousins who love seeing how things get built in the real world.

Rodrigo grew one of the largest e-commerce logistics startups in Brazil from zero to $60M in revenue running 100k orders/month across 10k SKUs as the first employee. Prev. CS at UChicago, MBA from Chicago Booth.

Oscar led process optimization at Intel, Amazon, and J&J, and deployed AI for the U.S. government. Prev. Operations Research at Stanford and Georgia Tech.

**Ask**

Intros to decision makers at manufacturers, distributors, and retailers.

launches.tagline: Field Robots Faster with ATC Deploy
launches.body:
Today we're sharing Agency Tool Company and our first product, ATC Deploy: a faster, more reliable way to ship software to robots wherever they are. It moves updates up to 20 times faster than docker pull or scp and works with any software stack already in use.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jx0rLRVa06s>

## The updates that took until 2 a.m.

Davis and I spent eight years building Scythe Robotics and putting hundreds of autonomous mowers to work across the country. For years, we deployed software with a tool I'd cobbled together for our first few robots. As the fleet grew, deployment became an ordeal: engineers stayed up until 2 a.m., we coordinated with customers to move robots out of sheds and into LTE coverage at set times, and failed transfers restarted from zero. Shipping a fix could take more coordination than building it. We had models to train and customers to serve, so the tooling limped along with incremental bandaids.

We've since heard the same story from robotics teams across industries. That deployment becomes a hidden bottleneck: teams become release-averse, feedback loops slow and improvements stall. Stitched-together web and IoT tools barely work if you know which scripts to run and who to call, so they survive, even if it means every update is distracting from improving the product.

## What we built

ATC Deploy ships whatever you already run: OS images, Docker images, or any file tree. Run “atc ota push user@robot”, and it sends only the changed bytes, then restarts your software through hooks you define—way faster than a docker push.

Install takes one “curl | sh” command and a config file so you can get back to work fast. Interrupted transfers resume where they stopped, and an offline robot can receive updates by USB if you need. There's no new runtime, packaging format, or operating system to adopt.

## Shipping to robots today

ATC Deploy already ships software to robots at Burro, which has deployed more than 750 machines worldwide, Tempo, polishing concrete across several US states and Canada, and Gather, who is scaling their 99.9% accurate inventory drones nationwide. Their teams spend less time managing delivery and more time improving the robot.

**Operate a robot fleet? Join the ATC Deploy waitlist at [agencytool.com](https://agencytool.com/).** Know a team that should be using it? Send them this post, or to [mailbox@agencytool.com](mailto:mailbox@agencytool.com).

It's time to build robots.

launches.tagline: Deploy AI that owns complete jobs and are measured against predefined outcomes and KPIs. Tenor's AI operates across your tools and improves its decisions with every outcome to drive better results.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:**

The defining resource of the internet was page views. The defining resource of AI is tokens. But while companies can measure exactly what their tokens cost, they still can’t easily tell what those tokens produced. \
Tenor connects the two. Every piece of AI work starts with an outcome and a budget. Tenor tracks the resources spent against the result produced, learns from that result, and helps determine where the next tokens should go.\
That’s the bigger opportunity: not just attributing AI spend, but allocating machine intelligence toward what creates value. Once a company knows where its tokens make money, it can do more of what works, less of what doesn’t, and continuously reshape itself around where AI creates value.

<https://youtu.be/rRaLDa9yvC8>

## 🤯 The Problem

While companies have become good at measuring AI consumption, they still can’t tell what that intelligence produced in business value.\
\
The internet went through a similar transition.

Its defining resource was page views. Early on, advertisers could buy impressions and measure exposure. Search advertising changed the model by connecting spend to intent and outcomes. Google then turned that into an engine for allocating dollars toward what performed.

AI is still early in that transition. Companies deploy copilots, agents, and automations across the organization. Each produces activity and consumes tokens. But the economic context usually lives somewhere else.

What was this intelligence supposed to accomplish? What changed because it ran? Was the outcome worth what it cost? Should the next token go here or somewhere else?

Without those answers, AI remains largely a software expense: something companies buy and monitor rather than a resource they can economically allocate.

And the bigger loss isn’t wasted tokens. It’s lost learning.

Millions of pieces of work happen, outcomes disappear into different systems, and very little of that experience determines how the next unit of intelligence gets deployed.

### ⚙️ The Solution

Tenor starts with the outcome.

Before intelligence is deployed, the work gets an economic identity: what it owns, what success means, what it can spend, which systems it can act on, and when humans need to intervene.

Now every token is spent in service of something measurable.

So instead of: This agent consumed X.

You can ask: What did X produce?

That closes the loop: allocate → work → outcome → attribute → learn → reallocate

Attribution tells you what worked. Allocation is what makes that knowledge valuable.

Work that produces value can receive more intelligence. Work that doesn’t can be changed, rebuilt, or stopped. Every outcome improves the next allocation decision.

Over time, that feedback loop reaches beyond individual workflows.

Responsibilities move. Processes disappear. New ones emerge. Software changes around the work. The organization gradually restructures itself around where machine intelligence produces the greatest value.

That’s what we’re building Tenor for: not just to measure the token economy, but to give companies the machinery to operate inside it.

## 👋 Team

Muhtasham Oblokulov — AI researcher, 3,000+ citations, ICML-published. Former Senior ML Engineer at Munich Re, where his models drove $1B in revenue.

Hamze Al-Zamkan — President of [TUM.ai](http://TUM.ai), which he grew into Europe's largest student-led AI organization and a talent pipeline for Munich's AI ecosystem. Deployed AI systems at appliedAI, and worked on growth at Voggt and Terra. Studied CS at TUM and CDTM.

Amgad Al-Zamkan — Studied CS at TUM and UC Berkeley. Researched adaptive decision systems. Automated judgment-heavy work at Amazon.

## 🙏 Our Ask

If your AI spend is growing and your company isn't visibly getting better at its work every week, that gap is our market.
